neighbours.label: beliefs about the dead returning or persisting: 'the spirits of the dead', 'believed X to be a reincarnation of', the afterlife
fire: Many families believed that the spirits of the dead returned home on the last night of the harvest.
The monks believed the young boy to be a reincarnation of their late teacher.
In the old religion, the souls of the dead watched over the village from the hills.
The islanders thought the white sailor to be the returned ghost of a drowned chief.
Offerings of food were left at the grave so that the spirits of the ancestors would not go hungry.
The priests taught that the soul of the dead pharaoh would travel through the underworld.
Some villagers believed the old woman to be the reincarnation of a famous healer.
On that night, people say, the spirits of the departed walk among the living.
quiet: Many families believed that their relatives would return home on the last night of the harvest.
The monks believed the young boy to be a gifted student of their teacher.
In the old kingdom, the soldiers watched over the village from the hills.
The islanders thought the white sailor to be a trader from a distant port.
Offerings of food were left at the market so that the poor families would not go hungry.
The priests taught that the young pharaoh would travel through the whole country.
Some villagers believed the old woman to be the best healer in the valley.
On that night, people say, the musicians walk among the crowd.

notes: Probe: 'believed the stranger to be a reincarnation of their dead chief' 0.40, 'the spirits of the dead' 0.30, 'through the afterlife' 0.15. Ghosts in an attic (0.04) and a wizard and magic (0.08) were low, so the label is narrowed from 'supernatural' to beliefs about the dead. Near misses keep the frames with living people.
